unit: 1.0 = one AssemblerComponent-type machine (incl. its power consumer) updated once per logic tick, vanilla game; costs are per entity per tick, independent of utilisation

unit_time_estimate_us.kind: CPU time (summed over threads) per unit per tick; wall-clock ~= value / effective threads
unit_time_estimate_us.source: GPUOpen devlog 6.8M universe matrix/min save (~0.8e7-1.6e7 units): i9-14900K 170 ms (pre-opt), TR PRO 9985WX 43-46 ms after opt; consistent with 'each Assembler a few hundred to a few thousand ns'. devtrackers '100 K Matrix save, 80 ms' is an outlier (rate, CPU, framework unstated) and not used. 'non-critical frame time' scope unknown. Only relative weights matter for the MILP.

sorter.note: non-bidirectional path, any grade. Used only via per_machine_terms (not a recipe building, so not in building_weights).
sorter.source: low end: x = s/(m*k), sorters 1/6 of a 22 ms frame (GPUOpen devlog), k=3, machine share m unknown; high end: 笑笑 ep18 16:52/19:18 panel shows belts+sorters larger than machines (needs x >= ~0.3-0.5). Planner choices unchanged for 0.12/0.4/0.6 (scripts/prolif_modes.py).

sorter_bidirectional.note: vanilla InternalUpdate_Bidirectional (Weaver UnOptimizedPlanetWorkChunk.cs 860-870, OptimizedBiInserter.cs): no travel timers or Delay, polls belt/machine every tick except idleTick backoff. Possibly pile sorters; bidirectional assignment 存疑.

per_machine_terms.sorters_per_machine: sum over input/output ports of ceil(port_rate_per_machine / sorter_capacity) = port count in practice. Mixed belts: a global PlanSettings flag that merges all inputs into one port (not an LP mode: it would always win). Direct insertion: not modelled.

sorter_capacity_items_per_s.note: capped at belt max (Mk.III x4 stack = 120 items/s); sorter's own capacity from calculators-survey.md 2.1.2 is 存疑. Result: k_r = port count in practice

spray_coaters_per_machine.note: 1 coater per input belt, ~10 machines per belt

belt_per_machine.note: belt segments (6-10 per machine x 0.002) plus share of belt paths; belts scale with machine count and layout, not flow

station_per_machine.note: planetary station cost 3 / M machines per station, M = 30 (笑笑 ep19 50:05)

per_machine_terms.implementation: Step 1: building_weights from buildings + Custom objective (buildings 1.0, power = generation.cost_per_mw). Step 2: Mode.aux_cost = sorter*k_r + belt + station + spray*s_r, objective w.buildings*(building_weight + aux_cost)*scale. Do not put aux in build_scaled's scale (multiplier, overwritten each heuristic round).

notes: Cost is per entity, not per unit of work: idle or blocked entities cost the same in vanilla (vanilla call layer confirmed via Weaver UnOptimizedPlanetWorkChunk.cs; sleep states are a Weaver addition).
Sorter count is first-order; sorter state second-order, except the bidirectional path which polls every tick.
Proliferator: per-recipe choice by the solver (products mode compounds upstream x0.8 per level; speed halves only the level); never fix 'speed' globally.
Belts and stations scale with machine count, so the objective is close to min-buildings with these weights plus a generation term.
Only relative weights matter for the MILP optimum; absolute time conversion is order-of-magnitude only.
Not modelled: Dyson swarm sails, Dark Fog combat, local-planet rendering, mining.

All coefficients except the assembler-class baseline are estimates; first to calibrate: sorter:machine ratio (normal vs pile sorter), in sandbox with chests (belts and sorters share one performance-panel category).

generation.note: objective term c_gen * sum p_r (MW); proliferator modes multiply power by 2.5. With wind/solar this term dominates (10k universe matrix/min ~57 GW -> ~2.8e4 units with wind vs ~1.2e4 for machines+sorters).

example_10k_universe_matrix.basis: machines + sorters 0.12/port; excludes mining, belts, stations, ray receivers, coaters, generation, research-consuming labs
